correctness.rationale: For n>q, any nonunique pirate mark received by s users forces all s recipients to receive globally unique marks next; otherwise the coalition of all other users can frame one recipient over two consecutive segments. The remaining n-s users then create a next nonunique class of size at least ceil((n-s)/(q-s)). If n exceeds max_s s(q-s+1), these class sizes strictly increase until impossible. The explicit size-a class construction attains a(q-a+1), and maximizing over a gives floor((q+1)^2/4). Finite exhaustive checks for q<=6 agree with the construction.

originality.rationale: Paterson's 2007 sliding-window paper explicitly asks whether fully general schemes with segment-dependent protection can outperform the restricted constructions. The l=2 specialization of the known construction gives a(q-a+1), but no unrestricted exact upper bound was located. Searches across sliding-window dynamic frameproof, dynamic frameproof, window-two, and static/wide-sense variants, together with the 2026 citation-index snapshot for the primary paper, revealed no source stating the exact unrestricted formula.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly resolves the first nontrivial sliding-window length in the unrestricted model, sharpens the general O(q^2) scale to an exact floor((q+1)^2/4), and supplies a simple local mechanism explaining why arbitrary feedback-dependent variation cannot beat the balanced fixed-size construction.
